title: build.rs silently tolerates a missing API bundle; release must assert it exists
answers: posthog-cli builds fine but api subcommand does nothing
Why does publish-cargo verify the bundle is non-empty?
Where does the posthog-cli api bundle come from in a release?
body:
cli/build.rs emits `EMBEDDED_API_CLI_BUNDLE: Option<&[u8]> = None` when lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs is missing, and still compiles. A missing bundle therefore never fails the build; it just ships a dead `posthog-cli api`.
- The publish-cargo job in .github/workflows/release-cli.yml guards this with `test -s cli/lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs` (step 'Verify the bundle is present') before publishing. Keep that check in any new publish path.
- The bundle is extracted from the release's posthog-cli-npm-package.tar.gz (package/lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs) rather than rebuilt from services/mcp, so all channels ship identical bytes. A reviewer confirmed the npm archive does contain it (~8.6MB), and `tar` exits non-zero if it is absent.
applies: Any release channel or build that packages posthog-cli with the embedded API bundle
